# An invoice applying both suspense splits of one arrival.
#
# Neither split is on the receivable yet, and the invoice does not post to
# `Assets:Suspense USD`. What allows it is the account: money waits in a
# suspense account, and a `Transaction` block says which splits of the
# arrival are this invoice's. Both move to the receivable and come to the
# 100.00 it is owed.
#
# This is the invoice side of the grouped spelling. The bill side needs the
# posting to book the account because the split there is a cost; a suspense
# split is money, and money waiting to be identified has always been movable.
#
# What this fixture produces: the invoice settled, both splits on the
# receivable and in its lot.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
invoice "INV-USD-001"
  customer_id: "C-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-01-05
  entry:
    date: 2026-01-05
    description: "Consulting"
    action: "Hours"
    account: "Income:Sales"
    quantity: 1
    price: 100
    taxable: false
    tax_included: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-01-05
    due: 2026-02-05
    ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
    memo: "Invoice INV-USD-001"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-03-10
    amount: 100
    account: "Assets:Bank:USD"
    Transaction "8a9b0cddeeff00112233aabb4c5d6e7f"
      PaymentSplit "0cddeeff00112233aabb4c5d6e7f8a9b"
      PaymentSplit "cddeeff00112233aabb4c5d6e7f8a9b0"
